detailed_rationale:
HCLTech's Q1 FY27 print (reported 13 July 2026, quarter ended June 2026) was a mixed-quality beat. Revenue came in at Rs 34,579 crore / $3.65bn, up 13.9% YoY in rupee terms but only 2.6-3.0% YoY in constant currency (CC) - and CC revenue was actually down 0.5-0.9% sequentially, i.e. the quarter shrank in dollar terms versus March. Net profit rose a stronger 20.3% YoY to Rs 4,624 crore, driven by EBIT margin expanding to 16.9% reported (17.5% ex-restructuring, versus a 122bps restructuring drag a year ago easing to 62bps) - a genuine operating-leverage improvement, not a one-off tax or forex gain; profit outgrowing revenue is explained cleanly by the margin build, so no adjustment is needed there. Management retained FY27 guidance exactly as before: revenue growth of 1-4% CC (services 1.5-4.5%) and EBIT margin of 17.5-18.5%. Net-new deal bookings of $2.407bn were the highest-ever Q1 total, above the trailing four-quarter average of $2.2bn, plus a separately flagged mega-deal near $1.14bn - a genuinely strong demand signal - but the gap between record TCV and flat-to-negative CC revenue growth is the same deal-to-revenue conversion lag the desk has flagged industry-wide; large-deal ramp cycles are running slower than the bookings headline suggests.

Underneath the headline, the mix tells a more cautious story. HCLSoftware - the higher-margin product arm that has historically been HCLTech's differentiator versus TCS/Infosys - declined 5.3% YoY in CC with segment EBIT margin compressing sharply from 22.4% to 17.6%; Telecom & Media was the weakest vertical at -10.9% YoY, and ER&D stayed soft (roughly -3.7%). Against that, BFSI (+5.3%), Retail & CPG (+10.1%) and Technology & Services (+7.3%) grew well, so six of seven verticals were still up YoY - this is a mix problem, not a broad-based demand collapse. Advanced AI/GenAI revenue reached $171mn, up 62.1% YoY CC and 10.6% QoQ, and management is targeting roughly 30% sustained annual growth in that book - the clearest structural positive in the print. But the same management explicitly quantified AI-led deflation/pricing pressure across the broader services portfolio at an estimated 2-3%, which they say will be offset by new AI-transformation, infrastructure and engineering demand - an offset that is asserted, not yet proven in the numbers. FY27 also brought a real strategic pivot: a ~Rs 3,500 crore (~$365-400mn) commitment to build and operate owned AI data-center infrastructure, a departure from HCLTech's traditionally asset-light, high-payout model, with no disclosed payback timeline or return profile yet - a capital-allocation watch-item for a company that has built its premium on capital discipline (90.6% payout ratio, near-zero debt).

On reverse DCF: at Rs 1,204 (market cap ~Rs 3,26,700 crore) the stock trades at roughly 18.0x trailing earnings - near its own 10-year median multiple and materially below what a genuine re-rating to a higher-growth story would require. Dividend yield of 4.49% on a 90%+ payout, ROE of ~24% and ROCE of ~30.6% with an almost debt-free balance sheet are all consistent with the market pricing HCLTech as a mature, cash-returning compounder, not a hypergrowth name - which is the correct framing given a guided 1-4% CC FY27. The multiple does not look stretched against that guidance; it also does not look cheap enough to compensate for the real, company-specific soft spots (Software segment decline, unproven data-center capex, GenAI-deflation offset not yet demonstrated in the numbers) layered on top of a sector-wide guidance reset that is compressing growth expectations across all of large-cap IT this cycle.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, not Sell: there is no balance-sheet, governance or capital-return red flag here - ROE 24%, ROCE 30.6%, near-zero debt, 90%+ payout and a 4.49% dividend yield are all intact, and six of seven verticals still grew YoY with record net-new bookings. The valuation (18x, near 10-year median) is not pricing aggressive growth, so there isn't a rich-multiple-versus-decelerating-business mismatch severe enough to justify Sell on its own. Hold, not a stronger call either: FY27 guidance of just 1-4% CC growth is a genuine deceleration from HCLTech's own 3-year revenue CAGR (8.65% per the quant base) and 5-year sales CAGR (~12%, screener.in), the HCLSoftware decline (-5.3% YoY CC, margin down ~480bps) removes the company's historical differentiator versus peers for now, the 2-3% GenAI deflation is a real and unresolved pricing headwind, and the new data-center capex commitment adds execution/capital-allocation risk without a disclosed return profile. None of that is severe enough to sell a quality, well-capitalised compounder, but none of it is strong enough to add exposure into either. This also sits inside a sector-wide guidance-reset cycle (per house note: large-cap IT guidance resets move the whole group) rather than being an HCLTech-specific failure, which further argues against a company-specific Sell call.
summary: HCL Technologies delivered a solid Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) on profit and margins - net profit up 20% YoY to Rs 4,624 crore, with margins improving - and logged its highest-ever first-quarter deal bookings of $2.4 billion. But underlying dollar revenue growth was just 2.6-3% year-on-year and actually shrank slightly versus the prior quarter, management kept its already-modest full-year growth guidance of 1-4% unchanged, and the company's higher-margin software business shrank 5.3% with a meaningful margin hit. Management also flagged that AI-driven pricing pressure is trimming 2-3% off its existing business, an effect it hopes new AI-related work will offset but hasn't yet proven out, and it committed roughly Rs 3,500 crore to build its own AI data centres - a departure from its traditionally asset-light, high-payout model, with no disclosed payback timeline. At about 18 times earnings - near the stock's own long-term average - the market isn't overpaying for growth it may not get, but nor is the stock cheap enough to look like a clear opportunity given the real, company-specific soft spots layered on top of an industry-wide slowdown in growth guidance. We rate it a Hold: a well-run, well-capitalised, dividend-paying business going through a genuine growth air-pocket, not a name we'd add to or exit from at current levels.
positive_para: HCLTech remains one of the highest-quality balance sheets in Indian IT services: ROE of ~24%, ROCE of ~30.6%, near-zero debt, and a payout ratio above 90% translating into a 4.49% dividend yield at current prices - this is a business that returns cash reliably rather than one dependent on re-rating for total return. The demand funnel looks genuinely healthy: net-new bookings of $2.407bn were the highest-ever Q1 total (above the trailing four-quarter average), plus a further ~$1.14bn mega-deal, and six of seven verticals grew YoY, with BFSI (+5.3%) and Retail & CPG (+10.1%) particularly strong - this is broad-based demand, not one lucky deal. The clearest structural positive is Advanced AI/GenAI revenue, which hit $171mn and grew 62.1% YoY in constant currency (10.6% QoQ), with management targeting roughly 30% sustained annual growth in that line - if that trajectory holds, it becomes a genuine second growth engine layered on top of the core services base. EBIT margin also expanded to 16.9% (17.5% ex-restructuring) even with unfavorable mix, and management reaffirmed its 17.5-18.5% FY27 margin band unchanged, signalling confidence in cost and pyramid discipline despite the software-segment drag. At ~18x earnings - near the stock's own 10-year median - none of this quality or momentum is being paid for at a stretched multiple.
negative_para: The bear case, and the one we take most seriously, is the same one flagging brokerages (Citi among them) have made: a business whose higher-margin differentiator, HCLSoftware, just shrank 5.3% YoY in constant currency with segment margin collapsing from 22.4% to 17.6%, sitting underneath unchanged, already-modest FY27 guidance of just 1-4% CC growth - a guidance band management chose not to raise even after a record bookings quarter. That gap between record TCV ($2.4bn+) and flat-to-negative sequential CC revenue is a genuine deal-to-revenue conversion problem, not just a reporting artifact: large-deal ramp cycles are running slower than the bookings headline implies, and the FY27 guide effectively requires a back-half acceleration that is not yet visible in the numbers. Management's own estimate of 2-3% AI-led deflation across the existing portfolio is a real, structural pricing headwind to the base services business, and their claim that new AI-transformation work will offset it is an assertion the company has not yet demonstrated - Advanced AI at $171mn is still under 5% of total revenue, too small this year to fully offset deflation across a $14.6bn (annualized) base. Layered on top, the ~Rs 3,500 crore commitment to build owned AI data centres is a real strategic pivot away from the asset-light, high-payout model that has underpinned HCLTech's premium valuation and capital discipline for years, with no disclosed return profile or payback timeline - a capital-allocation risk the market has not yet had to price. Telecom & Media (-10.9%) and ER&D softness add to the sense that this is a genuinely uneven demand environment, not a one-quarter blip, and headcount fell a net 3,292 even as attrition ticked up to 12.7% TTM - a combination that could read as healthy automation-driven productivity or as a supply-side response to soft underlying demand; the data alone doesn't settle which.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~18x trailing earnings (Rs 1,204/share, ~Rs 3,26,700 crore market cap) - near HCLTech's own 10-year median multiple - the market is pricing a mature, high-payout, cash-returning IT compounder, not a growth stock: a 4.49% dividend yield on a 90%+ payout ratio is not consistent with an equity priced for acceleration. That framing is roughly right given FY27 guidance of just 1-4% CC revenue growth. The multiple therefore isn't obviously rich against near-term guidance, but it also isn't cheap enough to offer real margin of safety against the company-specific risks now visible in the mix (HCLSoftware in decline with a ~480bps margin hit, an unproven and capital-intensive data-center pivot, and a GenAI-deflation headwind the company has quantified but not yet shown it can outrun with new AI revenue). Verdict: fair, not cheap and not rich - a business priced in line with what it can currently deliver, with the multiple offering little cushion if the software/ER&D softness or the AI-deflation drag proves more durable than management's offset narrative assumes.
